week_in_brief: Healthcare marketers are navigating a patient acquisition crunch as paid search costs spike and organic search behavior shifts toward AI-generated answers.

items.headline: Google's AI Overviews are capturing 40%+ of informational health queries before the patient ever clicks
items.tag: 🔍 SEO | AI Overviews Are Rerouting Patient Search Journeys
items.whats_happening: New click-through data shows AI Overviews are dramatically reducing organic clicks on high-volume informational health queries ("symptoms of," "what is," "how to treat"). Clinics and health systems built around top-of-funnel blog content are seeing traffic erosion.
items.so_what: Shift your SEO content strategy toward bottom-of-funnel and local intent — queries like "cardiologist near me" and "urgent care [city]" are still driving clicks. The informational layer is increasingly owned by AI. Your content dollars work harder at the conversion end.

items.headline: Healthcare paid search CPCs averaged $18.40 in Q1 2026, up 27% YoY — with cardiology and orthopedics leading the surge
items.tag: 💊 PAID SEARCH | Healthcare CPCs Hit Record Highs in Q1
items.whats_happening: Competition from private equity-backed health systems and telehealth incumbents is driving up auction prices across nearly every specialty. Small and mid-size practices are getting priced out of branded competitor terms.
items.so_what: Audit your client's keyword mix for efficiency, not just volume. Branded terms and hyper-local modifiers are often 3–4x more efficient than broad specialty terms. If you're bidding on "orthopedic surgeon," you're fighting the whole market. "Orthopedic surgeon [neighborhood]" is a different auction.

items.headline: Health systems report 3x higher ROI on lapsed patient re-engagement vs. new patient acquisition campaigns
items.tag: 📧 CRM | Patient Re-engagement Campaigns Outperform Acquisition 3:1
items.whats_happening: Marketers who have shifted budget from acquisition to re-engagement — particularly for patients who haven't been seen in 12–24 months — are seeing significantly better returns. Preventive care reminders and annual wellness outreach are the top performers.
items.so_what: For clinic clients with a CRM or EMR integration, this is the lowest-hanging fruit. A well-segmented re-engagement sequence targeting lapsed patients is cheaper to run and converts better than cold acquisition. If they don't have this built, it's a clear recommendation.

this_weeks_take: Healthcare marketing is in a bifurcation moment. The broad, volume-based playbook — heavy informational SEO, broad paid search, general awareness — is getting more expensive and less effective simultaneously. The marketers winning right now are the ones going narrow and deep: local intent, lapsed patient reactivation, and specialty-specific content that AI can't easily summarize away. Specificity is the moat.
